notes: All 35 complete card pairs and their approved unsaved corrections were read directly against retained source and resolved judgments; categorical claims, conditional premises, and critical burdens remain distinct from evaluator conclusions.

Descriptions average 25.3 words, above both the independent hard floor and the stricter frozen 23.6-word recent-corpus target; no card is shorter than twenty words. Critiques average 127.2 words and 975.7 characters with no recurring six-word boilerplate at the defined threshold.

Both AI sides and all eight novelty explanations were reviewed together. The pro paragraphs compare explanatory economy, the distribution of hiddenness, and historical hypotheses; the con paragraphs distinguish prospective tests, justification of harm, and evidential dependence.

Substantive opening variation follows each argument rather than cosmetic variation: imperatives, a freedom-based conditional, a moral distinction, and a source-dependence proposition. The final arguments retain explicit conditional conclusions and no field announces its AI provenance.

All exposition-depth measures now fall within the independent reference window. Only the neutral motion length, prelocked structural coverage, and clean exact quote length remain justified source-led outliers.

The catalogue-wide punctuation screen covers 270 debates with no flagged outliers. The target punctuation density is close to the corpus median, and direct sentence review confirms intact clauses, lists, and qualifications.
